summary: Set 109 Session 2 of 4, "Routing transparency -- what actually gets called". THE TWO-METRICS-ROW ANOMALY IS RESOLVED, AND IT WAS THE WORSE-SOUNDING BUT BETTER-OUTCOME HYPOTHESIS: a REAL second call, not a duplicated or mis-attributed row. The metrics ledger was accurate the whole time and the ROUTER's behaviour was wrong -- a defect in what we did, not in what we know. Proved by counting at the boundary rather than reading the log, which is what the spec insisted on: a live traced `route(task_type="architecture", exclude_providers=["anthropic"])` at tier 3 issued TWO HTTPS POSTs -- `openai/gpt-5.4` then `anthropic/claude-opus-4-8` -- reproducing the spec's exact two rows (same models, providers, tiers, and the score/score=None asymmetry that made the second look orphaned). The barred call cost $0.0472 against the generator's $0.0097, 4.9x the call it was verifying. Post-fix the same call issues ONE request and comes back unverified. THREE SITES DROPPED THE CALLER'S EXCLUSION on the secondary calls route() makes on the caller's behalf (L-069-1): `_run_verification` (no exclude_providers parameter at all -- live, reproduced), the copilot-cli sibling `_run_verification_via_copilot_cli` -> `pick_copilot_cli_verifier` (LIVE ON A COPILOT SEAT, and the routed analyst's sibling list did not name it -- found by grepping the sibling profile for the same shape, where the GENERATOR was resolved against the exclusion and the VERIFIER against nothing), and `_tiebreaker_reroute` (hardcoded `opus`, latent since no configured on_disagreement is re-route). Both verifier selectors ALREADY accepted and correctly applied an exclusion; nothing was missing from selection logic, the constraint just stopped at the boundary between "the call route() makes" and "the call route() makes on your behalf". Fixes thread the caller's list through, seeding it into the accumulator the retry path already used so a FALLBACK attempt cannot re-cross it either; the excluded tiebreaker degrades into the branch that already existed for an unregistered tiebreaker (removal-first: a reachability gap closed, not a second selector added). VERIFICATION WAS NEVER AFFECTED, and this is recorded as a finding in its own right per the spec: verify_session and the close backstop both route `session-verification`, which is NOT in auto_verify_task_types, so neither ever entered the leaking branch -- now asserted by three tests (including one that fails if session-verification is ever added to that list, and one driving the real verify_session._default_route seam) rather than left as a reading of the config. BEHAVIOUR CHANGE, DECLARED: when the exclusion leaves no eligible verifier, route() proceeds unverified (the contract it already had). On the current registry that is confined to TIER 3 -- rule 1 bars the generator's own provider, the tier-distance rule admits only tiers 3-4, and every other tier-3 entry is Anthropic -- so tier-3 architecture calls under an Anthropic exclusion now come back unverified rather than Anthropic-verified. Tier 2 is unaffected and still auto-verifies on a permitted provider. Session 4 changes exactly that registry shape. A SECOND DEFECT CLASS, HANDED OVER BY S1, TURNED OUT TO BE FOUR SITES: routing could send work to a model the registry DISABLES, contradicting the identity-only contract S1 established for `is_enabled: false` (claude-opus-5 / claude-sonnet-5 sit in the registry on those terms). S1 named one; a pattern sweep found two more -- `pick_model`'s tier_assignments branch (governing every NON-pinned call) and `get_escalation_model` (where escalation became a way around a rule the initial pick enforced) -- and this session's OWN verification round found a fourth in `_tiebreaker_reroute`, which was invisible to the sweep because it had no is_enabled check at all and a grep for a defective check cannot match code that omits the check entirely. All four fixed, three by deletion. INSTRUMENTATION SHIPPED: `ai_router/call_trace.py`, a ContextVar-scoped record of provider HTTP requests announced INSIDE each caller (below call_model's retry loop, so a retry counts as the separate request it is), recording the id put on the wire rather than the local alias. THE HARNESS FALSIFIED TWO OF MY OWN CLAIMS, both corrected rather than argued: (1) "one row per request" is FALSE -- an escalation issues two requests and records one row by design -- so the suite pins the directional invariant instead (every provider a row names must be one the router actually called), qualified to traced api-profile calls because Copilot rows exist with zero trace entries; (2) my first falsifier check proved NOTHING because `git checkout <file>` restores from the INDEX and the work was already staged, silently restoring the fixed files. Re-run with `git checkout HEAD --`: 9 of 27 new tests fail pre-fix, all 27 pass restored. VERIFICATION: discovery round 1, 2-way fan-out on identical bundles, verifier gpt-5-6 on both arms with anthropic excluded via model-registry resolution -- VERIFIED, 0 blocking findings, $0.3864. Seven nits, three raised independently by BOTH arms. All seven were FIXED rather than merely recorded, because three were factual errors in this session's own evidence (stale test counts), one was a real code gap (the fourth is_enabled site), and three were documentation overclaims (dispatch vs transmission, the containment invariant, ContextVar isolation under asyncio). One nit was right in substance but its suggested assertion was wrong: `len(calls) == 1` holds only at tier 3, so the reproduction was split into both tier shapes, each asserting its own exact counts -- which also exposed that the mock was silently escalating (output_tokens 5 under the config's min 30), now an explicit knob. SUITE: 3257 passed, 6 skipped, 8 deselected, 0 failed (23m32s), run twice (3254 pre-remediation, 3257 after), delta from S1's 3230 baseline being exactly the 27 new tests with no existing test changed, removed, or newly skipped. Gates: drift_guard OK, tutorial_gate OK, guidance_report OK (10,895/12,000), model_inventory --check still exits 1 on S1's gpt-5.6 specimen by design. Router-side only, [Unreleased] in the changelog -- no version bump, no publish, no extension work.

reason.specifics: Recorded as the ROUTED analyst's recommendation (s2-ai-assignment-analysis.json), per the repo rule never to self-opine on model choice; the engine switch is the operator's call and costs a fresh seat/context, so it should be a deliberate decision rather than a default. Its reasoning: Session 3 designs a pricing schema, plans a scrape over three published pricing pages, and extracts structure from unstructured HTML -- parsing-heavy work whose output has a strong falsifier, since per-provider fixtures either parse or they do not. Three facts this session adds for the operator to weigh: (1) S3's deliverable is a PROPOSAL flow with a hard human-confirmation rule, so a parse failure must produce no proposal at all rather than a partial one -- the failure mode matters more than raw parsing skill; (2) gpt-5-4 is already the de-facto verifier this set routes to under the standing Anthropic exclusion, so choosing it as orchestrator would put the same model on both sides of S3's work and cost this set its cross-provider independence; (3) the Copilot seat budget is very limited, so any engine switch draws on the DABBLER_* keys, not the seat. Continuing with claude / claude-opus-5 / high remains a defensible alternative on ground (2) alone.
